# SignalWire Documentation

> Build voice, video, messaging, and AI applications with SignalWire developer tools and implementation guides.

SignalWire is a programmable communications platform for building voice, video, messaging, and AI applications.
Start with the navigation and development interfaces below, then choose the path that matches your task.

## Navigate the documentation

- Treat the [root `llms.txt`](https://signalwire.com/docs/llms.txt) as an orientation page and directory, not an exhaustive list of documentation pages. The available documentation indexes appear under `## Products` at the bottom of the file.
- Fetch a documentation page as clean Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL or requesting it with the HTTP header `Accept: text/markdown`.
- Open the relevant documentation index to discover its page links.
- If a page is not listed in the root index, check the relevant documentation index before concluding that the documentation does not contain it.

## Development interfaces and tools

- [Server SDKs](/docs/server-sdks): Build and deploy AI agents, control calls through HTTP requests or real-time WebSocket connections, and send messages and manage platform resources through SignalWire's REST APIs. Available in multiple languages so you can integrate these capabilities into your application's backend.
- [Browser SDK](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/overview): Add voice, video, and chat to web applications, with controls for calls, participants, cameras, microphones, and screen sharing. Build a custom interface in JavaScript or embed prebuilt calling components.
- [REST APIs](/docs/apis): Place and control calls, send messages, and manage phone numbers, subscribers, video rooms, and logs through HTTP requests. Integrate communication and account administration into backend services, scripts, or any application that can call an HTTP API.
- [SignalWire Markup Language (SWML)](/docs/swml): Define call flows, message handling, and AI agent behavior in YAML or JSON, including prompts, routing, and replies. SignalWire executes the instructions from a hosted script or a document returned by your server.
- [SWSH (SignalWire interactive shell)](/docs/platform/swsh): Manage your Space from the terminal: configure phone numbers, place calls, send messages, and retrieve call records. Run commands interactively or incorporate them into shell scripts to automate repeated tasks.
- [WireStarter](/docs/platform/wirestarter): Run and test demo applications locally in a Docker environment with SignalWire SDKs and SWSH. Follow the guided setup to connect your Space and configure ngrok tunneling so SignalWire can reach the local applications.
- [Call Flow Builder](/docs/call-flow-builder): Create voice applications and AI call flows visually in the Dashboard. Connect nodes for greetings, caller input, routing, and AI conversations, then test and version the flows that SignalWire hosts and runs.
- [Compatibility API](/docs/compatibility-api): Migrate existing Twilio calling and messaging applications using TwiML-compatible XML instructions and REST endpoints. Adapt your application's credentials, API endpoints, and webhook configuration to run it on SignalWire.

## Choose a path

Find the task that matches what you want to build, how your application connects to SignalWire, or what you need to manage. Each task lists the interfaces and tools to use; their descriptions and documentation links are in Development interfaces and tools above.

### Learn the platform and get started

- [Get started](/docs/platform/getting-started): Walkthrough of your Space, the build paths, and the core concepts.
- [Create an account](/docs/platform/signing-up-for-a-space): Open a new Space on the SignalWire platform.
- [API credentials](/docs/platform/your-signalwire-api-space): Find the Project ID and API token that SDKs and APIs use to authenticate.
- [Resources](/docs/platform/resources): Communication entities such as AI agents, SignalWire Markup Language (SWML) scripts, Subscribers, and Video Rooms.
- [Addresses](/docs/platform/addresses): The aliases, phone numbers, and Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) URIs that make a Resource reachable.
- [Subscribers](/docs/platform/subscribers): Resources that represent users, and the basis of user management.
- [Phone numbers](/docs/platform/phone-numbers): Buy, port, and configure phone numbers.
- [Webhooks](/docs/platform/webhooks): Receive events about calls and messages over HTTP.

### Understand the communication channels

- [Calling](/docs/platform/calling): Voice, video, fax, and AI on one platform.
- [Voice](/docs/platform/voice): Programmable calling with integrated AI.
- [Video](/docs/platform/video): Programmable video conferencing.
- [Fax](/docs/platform/fax): Send and receive faxes.
- [Messaging](/docs/platform/messaging): Programmable Short Message Service (SMS) and Multimedia Messaging Service (MMS).
- [WhatsApp](/docs/platform/messaging/whatsapp): Send and receive WhatsApp messages.
- [Chat](/docs/platform/chat): Programmable chat for applications.
- [AI](/docs/platform/ai): Conversational agents directed by your code, data, and business rules.

### Run an AI agent in voice or text conversations

Define the agent's behavior and tools, then connect it to a phone number or text conversation. The [AI quickstart](/docs/platform/ai/quickstart) shows how one agent configuration can serve both voice and AI Chat.

- Server SDKs: [Build your first agent in code](/docs/server-sdks/guides/quickstart) and [add functions the agent can call](/docs/server-sdks/guides/swaig) to work with your backend.
- SWML: Define prompts, languages, and functions in an [AI configuration](/docs/swml/reference/calling/ai).
- Dashboard AI agent: [Create an AI Agent resource in the Dashboard](/docs/platform/resources#in-the-dashboard) and assign it a reachable address or phone number.

### Build a voice application with low-code or no-code tools and no server of your own

Host your call logic in SignalWire for flows such as greetings, menus, routing, and AI conversations. Choose a visual editor or a hosted script according to how you want to author the flow.

- Call Flow Builder: [Connect call-flow nodes in the Dashboard](/docs/call-flow-builder) to define branches and actions visually.
- SWML: [Create a hosted script and connect it to a phone number](/docs/swml/guides) so SignalWire runs the instructions when a call arrives.

### Send and receive SMS and MMS

Send text and media messages from your application, and choose how to process incoming messages. The [platform messaging overview](/docs/platform/messaging) covers setup, examples, and sender registration.

- Server SDKs: [Send SMS or MMS and track delivery](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/client/send-message), and register an incoming-message handler with the [Relay client](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/client).
- SWML: [Handle incoming SMS and MMS with a messaging document](/docs/swml/reference/messaging) and [send a reply](/docs/swml/reference/messaging/reply).
- REST APIs: [Send a message over HTTP](/docs/apis/rest/messages/create-message) and [receive delivery status callbacks](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/message-status-callback).

### Browser or mobile app calling and chat

Give users an identity, authorize their access, and connect them to other users or shared resources. Your backend manages subscribers and credentials; the client provides the calling and chat interface.

- Browser SDK: For web clients, [place audio or video calls](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/outbound-calls) and [send and display chat messages](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/messaging-chat).
- REST APIs: [Create subscribers](/docs/apis/rest/subscribers/create-subscriber) and [issue subscriber access tokens](/docs/apis/rest/subscribers/tokens/create-subscriber-token) from your backend. Follow the [Browser SDK authentication guide](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/authentication) to connect a web client.

### Video conferences

Build a browser conference interface or use a conference with a prebuilt interface. The [platform video overview](/docs/platform/video) explains rooms, participant permissions, and recordings.

- Browser SDK: [Join a room with audio and video](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/outbound-calls), then add [call controls](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/call-controls), [screen sharing](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/screen-sharing), and [participant layouts](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/layouts).
- REST APIs: [Create a video room](/docs/apis/rest/video/rooms/create-room) and [issue room access tokens](/docs/apis/rest/video/room-tokens/create-room-token), or [create a video conference with a prebuilt interface](/docs/apis/rest/video/video-conferences/create-video-conference).

### Migrate a Twilio application

- Compatibility API

### Provision and manage numbers, resources, subscribers, and logs

Automate account administration: buy numbers, manage communication resources and users, and query logs to investigate calls and messages.

- Server SDKs: Use the REST client to manage platform resources from application code. The [REST client reference](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/rest) includes examples for purchasing numbers, listing resources, and querying logs.
- REST APIs: [Purchase a phone number](/docs/apis/rest/phone-numbers/purchase-phone-number), [list resources](/docs/apis/rest/resources/list-resources), [create a subscriber](/docs/apis/rest/subscribers/create-subscriber), and query [voice logs](/docs/apis/rest/voice-logs/list-voice-logs) or [message logs](/docs/apis/rest/message-logs/list-message-logs).

### Act on a live call, or send a message, with a single HTTP request

Trigger a communication action from a backend job, webhook handler, or existing application. For call control, supply the active call's identifier and the command to perform.

- Server SDKs: Use the REST client's [call-control methods](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/rest/calling) to play audio, record, transfer, or end a call from your application.
- REST APIs: [Send a call command](/docs/apis/rest/calls/call-commands) or [send an SMS or MMS message](/docs/apis/rest/messages/create-message) directly over HTTP.

### Return call or messaging instructions from your server over HTTP, one synchronous request at a time

Use this approach when your application needs to decide what should happen when a call or message arrives. SignalWire requests instructions from your URL, your server returns a document, and SignalWire executes it.

- SWML: [Generate call instructions on your web server](/docs/swml/guides/remote-server), or return a [Messaging SWML document](/docs/swml/reference/messaging) to handle an incoming SMS or MMS.
- Server SDKs for AI agents: Use the [agent framework](/docs/server-sdks/guides/architecture) to generate SWML from your agent's configuration and serve it over HTTP.

### Handle communication over a persistent WebSocket connection, issuing commands and reacting to events asynchronously

Use an ongoing connection when your application needs to react to call events and issue commands throughout a conversation, such as playing prompts, collecting input, or changing participant controls.

- Server SDKs, Relay client: [Build an event-driven call handler](/docs/server-sdks/guides/relay-client) that answers calls and controls their flow from your backend.
- Browser SDK: [Handle incoming calls](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/inbound-calls) and [update call controls](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/call-controls) from the browser while observing call and participant state.

### Set up local development and testing

Try a working demo or develop your own agent locally, then give SignalWire a public URL for testing calls and webhooks.

- WireStarter: Follow the [Docker environment setup](/docs/platform/wirestarter) to run the bundled demos.
- Server SDKs: [Set up your development environment](/docs/server-sdks/guides/dev-environment), [run your first agent](/docs/server-sdks/guides/quickstart), and [expose its local HTTP server through a tunnel](/docs/server-sdks/guides/exposing-agents).

### Configure and manage a Space from the command line

Use SWSH for terminal-based administration and repeatable shell scripts, such as listing phone numbers or retrieving call records. The [SWSH command guide](/docs/platform/swsh) covers installation, credentials, and interactive or scripted commands.

## Popular features

Feature pages are grouped by channel. SDK pages come first when available, followed by SWML or platform pages when no SDK feature page exists.

### Calling

- [Call recording](/docs/swml/guides/record-calls): Record an ongoing call with a hosted SWML script and access the recording in your Space.
- [Call transfer](/docs/server-sdks/guides/call-transfer): Transfer a call to a phone number, SIP endpoint, or SWML document.
- [Real-time transcription](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/live-transcribe): Start or stop live transcription on a call.
- [Live translation](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/live-translate): Start or stop live translation on a call.
- [Audio streaming](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/stream): Stream call audio to a WebSocket endpoint.
- [Conferencing](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/join-conference): Join a call to an ad-hoc audio conference.
- [Secure payments](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/pay): Collect payment information on a call.
- [Collect caller input](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/play-and-collect): Play audio and collect speech or key presses.
- [Answering machine detection](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/detect): Detect answering machines, fax tones, or digits on a call.
- [Noise reduction](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/denoise): Start noise reduction on a call.
- [Call queues](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/queue-enter): Place a call into a named queue.
- [Text-to-speech voices](/docs/platform/voice/tts): Supported providers, voices, and languages.
- [Caller ID and Calling Name (CNAM)](/docs/platform/voice/how-to-set-caller-id-or-cnam): Configure an outbound number and a caller name that supported carriers can display.
- [STIR/SHAKEN caller verification](/docs/platform/voice/stir-shaken): STIR (Secure Telephone Identity Revisited) and SHAKEN (Secure Handling of Asserted information using toKENs) provide caller identity attestation for outbound calls.
- [SIP](/docs/platform/voice/sip): SIP trunking, SIP credentials, and bring your own carrier.
- [Web Real-Time Communication (WebRTC)](/docs/platform/voice/what-is-webrtc): How SignalWire uses WebRTC for real-time media.

### Video

- [Voice and video in the browser](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/build-voice-video): Build a calling or video experience with the Browser SDK.
- [Screen sharing](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/screen-sharing): Share a screen in a video call.
- [Layouts and participant views](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/layouts): Arrange participants in a video call.
- [Device management](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/device-management): Choose cameras, microphones, and speakers.
- [Click-to-call widget](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/click-to-call-widget): Add a call button to a public web page.
- [Join a video room from a call](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/call/join-room): Join a video or audio room from a call.

### Messaging

- [Chat in the browser](/docs/browser-sdk/v4/guides/messaging-chat): Add messaging and chat to a browser app.
- [Send SMS and MMS](/docs/server-sdks/reference/python/relay/client/send-message): Send an outbound SMS or MMS message.
- [Campaign Registry registration for 10-digit long code (10DLC) numbers](/docs/platform/messaging/campaign-registry/registration): Register a brand and campaign for business SMS in the United States.
- [Toll-free verification](/docs/platform/messaging/toll-free-numbers): Verify a toll-free number for messaging.
- [Hosted messaging](/docs/platform/messaging/hosted-messaging): Port messaging service only to SignalWire.
- [Delivery best practices](/docs/platform/messaging/sms-best-practices): Improve message delivery rates.
- [Character limits](/docs/platform/messaging/character-limits): How message segments are measured and priced.
- [MIME types](/docs/platform/messaging/mime-types): Media types supported in MMS.

### AI

- [Tool calling with the SignalWire AI Gateway (SWAIG)](/docs/server-sdks/guides/swaig): Let the agent call functions on your backend through webhooks.
- [Skills](/docs/server-sdks/guides/understanding-skills): Add reusable capabilities to an agent without custom code.
- [Prompts and the Prompt Object Model (POM)](/docs/server-sdks/guides/prompts-pom): Build structured prompts with sections, subsections, and bullets.
- [Contexts and workflows](/docs/server-sdks/guides/contexts-workflows): Multi-step conversation flows with branching and validation.
- [DataMap](/docs/server-sdks/guides/data-map): Call REST APIs from the agent without running code on your server.
- [Search and knowledge](/docs/server-sdks/guides/search-knowledge): Add knowledge search to an agent with vector indexes.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Gateway](/docs/server-sdks/guides/mcp-gateway): Connect MCP servers to an agent.
- [Multi-agent servers](/docs/server-sdks/guides/multi-agent): Run several agents on one server.
- [Voice and language](/docs/server-sdks/guides/voice-language): Configure the agent's voice, language, and pronunciation.
- [AI sidecar](/docs/swml/reference/calling/ai-sidecar): Attach a real-time AI observer to a live call.
- [Prompt engineering](/docs/platform/ai/prompt-engineering): Where to place instructions and how to structure a prompt.
- [Conversation analytics](/docs/platform/ai/analytics): Analyze conversations with post-prompt reports and debug webhooks.
- [Sensitive content](/docs/platform/ai/content-redaction): Redact sensitive content from AI conversations.

[Create a SignalWire account](https://signalwire.com/signup), or follow the [Platform getting-started guide](/docs/platform/getting-started) to configure an existing Space.
